tips.title: Assembling Multi-Part Gun Barrels (Trumpeter, AFV Club)
tips.text: With Trumpeter and AFV Club kits, multi-part gun barrels can be challenging. Start by test-fitting parts to ensure a proper fit. Use tweezers to apply a tiny dot of CA glue (like Testors Clear) where parts join. Allow 30 seconds for parts to set, then use tweezers to gently press parts together. For a seamless fit, lightly sand joins with a fine grit sanding stick after gluing.

tips.title: Aligning Wings with a DIY Jig
tips.text: For kits like ICM or Meng, ensure wing alignment with a DIY jig. Cut a square slot in a scrap piece of wood matching wing root width. Insert the wing roots into the slot, ensuring the wings are level and parallel. Glue wings together using Tamiya Extra Thin Cement, clamping and weighing down until cured.

tips.title: Installing Eduard Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: Eduard photo-etch parts often require bending and shaping. Use a GodHand nipper to carefully cut and bend parts using the bend lines as a guide. For complex shapes, use a needle or pin to gradually bend parts, avoiding sudden force. Apply CA glue (like UHU Plus) to attach parts, allowing 30 seconds for setting before positioning.

tips.title: Working with Resin Conversion Kits (Clear Prop Models)
tips.text: Resin conversion kits require careful handling due to their fragility. Lightly sand mating surfaces with fine grit sandpaper before gluing with CA glue (like Loctite Super Glue). Test fit parts first to ensure a proper fit. If necessary, use a razor saw to trim excess resin.

tips.title: Assembling Workable Tracks (Arma Hobby)
tips.text: Arma Hobby's workable tracks require careful assembly. Soak individual links in warm water until they soften, then bend and connect them as per the instructions. To strengthen the track, use thin CA glue (like Loctite Super Glue) along the seam where links join, allowing them to set before handling. Once assembled, dip tracks in Vallejo Acrylic Thinner to remove any remaining lubricant.
